findings.passage: "Some of my colleagues argue that by further curtailing our Second Amendment rights, they can enhance public safety," he said. "Fine, the burden of proof is on them. I'm willing to have that debate, but I want the bacon without the sizzle -- no speculation, no false comfort, no pulling stuff out of your orifices."
findings.note: Quoted by Fox News (The Story interview). Says supporters of new limits must prove with evidence that a law would work.

findings.passage: "Our rights are not absolute," he added. "Our rights can be curtailed in the interest of public safety. All I'm saying is... prove it."
findings.note: Quoted by Fox News (The Story interview). Says gun rights can be limited for public safety if shown to work.

findings.passage: "Here is my starting point, Martha: I believe that love is the answer, but I also own a handgun just in case -- in fact I own several. Shotguns too," Kennedy told host Martha MacCallum.
findings.note: Quoted by Fox News. Says he owns guns and treats the Second Amendment like other rights.

findings.passage: "Beto's copy of the Bill of Rights goes from one to three," he said. "Mine includes the Second Amendment. But there are a whole host of people here in Washington... they would be happy to confiscate America's guns. And if you don't believe that, then you probably also still believe in Bigfoot. It's a fact, and everybody up here knows it."
findings.note: Quoted by Fox News (America's Newsroom). Responds to calls for assault-style rifle confiscation and red-flag laws.

findings.passage: "I wouldn't bet my house on it," he said. "And if I were betting your house... I'd probably say, maybe. We've got to see what the proposals are first. The president's opinion matters. I met with Bill Barr yesterday... They're looking at expanded background checks."
findings.note: Quoted by Fox News. Says he would wait to see proposals before judging; reports that the administration was looking at expanded background checks.

findings.passage: "Grassley and Cruz’s bill, which I support, would have tightened up the database, and it would have cracked down on people who have guns who shouldn’t have guns," Kennedy also said.
findings.note: Quoted by Just the News (Fox News interview). Supports a bill to strengthen the background-check database.

findings.passage: "In my judgment, we do not need more gun control, we need more idiot control," Kennedy also said.
findings.note: Quoted by Just the News. Opposes new gun control laws after two mass shootings.
